openItems.item: /christian-wedding and /christian-wedding-2 remain linked ZERO times across all 79 posts.
openItems.why: No wave-3 keyword SERP justifies them. `digital wedding invitation in marathi`, `digital invitation indian wedding` and every other wedding-invitation keyword screened returned 10/10 invitation-maker tool pages (Gate 2 fail for a blog). Forcing the link into the Hindu-shaadi post would have been a 5th internal link and an off-topic one. BRIEF-WAVE2 §2 is explicit that a wrong link is worse than an unbalanced batch.
openItems.fix: These two are a TOOL-PAGE opportunity, not a blog one - see strategicFinding below.

strategicFinding: The digital-invitation axis is a tool-page opportunity, not a blog opportunity. Of ~319 invitation keywords in the harvest, every occasion- and feature-shaped one returns 10/10 invitation-MAKER product pages (Canva, easyinvite.in, desievite.com, invitationbazaar, craftyartapp, Paperless Post, RSVPify). Only the definitional shape `what is a digital invitation` has a blog SERP (7/10 editorial), which is why it is the single invitation row in this wave. The correct action for the rest is landing-page SEO on /wedding-shaadi, /shaadi-card, /reception, /christian-wedding and /christian-wedding-2 - which currently rank nowhere - not blog posts.

abortedRows.reason: 9/10 organic URL overlap with the PUBLISHED wave-1 post `virtual gift for best friend`. Google returns essentially the same result set for both queries, so a second page would compete with one we already own. The wave-3 rule rejects at >=6/10.
abortedRows.intentDistinctionFound: An "online friend" is someone never met in person: no address can be asked for, real name/city/timezone may be unknown, and consent/safety is a live consideration. The distinction is real but the SERP does not reflect it.
abortedRows.recommendation: Add the never-met-friend angle as a SECTION to the existing virtual-gift-for-best-friend post rather than as its own page.

abortedRows.reason: Three independent grounds, found by the writing agent at Phase 2: (1) DECISIVE - `best online gift for girlfriend` is already declared in the secondaryKeywords of the published post online-gift-for-girlfriend, and the BRIEF forbids targeting another row's secondary; (2) the assigned differentiation lane was already published almost clause-for-clause in what-can-i-gift-my-girlfriend; (3) the SERP is 4/10 marketplace search pages + 3 physical-product affiliate listicles (Wirecutter #1) + 3 banned competitors - zero results a blog could displace.
abortedRows.whyItWasMissedInitially: ORCHESTRATOR BUG - my keyword dedupe did not stem. "best online gifts for girlfriend" vs the claimed "best online gift for girlfriend" scored only 0.60 Jaccard because gift/gifts are distinct tokens. With stemming it scores 1.00. See stemmingBug below.
abortedRows.alsoRevealed: The binding collision was TOPICAL (with what-can-i-gift-my-girlfriend), not URL-based. The plan had flagged a different post (online-creative-gift-ideas-for-girlfriend, 5/10 URL overlap). URL-overlap screening cannot see an angle collision.
abortedRows.phase3Skipped: Deliberately - aborting at Phase 2 avoided spending scarce Crossref/Unpaywall calls and a source-domain slot that siblings still drafting needed.

blindSpotPostMortem.finding: The initial anti-cannibalisation check compared wave-3 candidates only against SERPS-WAVE2.md, which holds SERPs for 28 of the 60 written posts. The other 32 (wave-1) had no SERP on record, so the ">=6/10 = duplicate" rule was structurally blind to them.
blindSpotPostMortem.howItSurfaced: A writing agent found an unflagged near-neighbour on its own and reported it. That prompted the audit.
blindSpotPostMortem.remediation: Backfilled all 32 missing SERPs with serp-ddg.mjs (kl=in-en) into SERPS-WAVE1-BACKFILL.md and re-ran the check across all 60 written posts.
blindSpotPostMortem.caught: 1 outright duplicate (virtual-gift-for-online-friend, 9/10) aborted mid-write; 3 additional rows newly flagged as needing differentiation against wave-1 posts that were previously invisible: best-virtual-gift-for-boyfriend (4/10 vs virtual gift for best friend), surprise-website-for-girlfriend-free (4/10 vs how to surprise girlfriend online), online-gift-maker-for-gf (4/10 vs virtual christmas gift for girlfriend).
blindSpotPostMortem.lessonForNextWave: Record a SERP for EVERY post at write time. A batch that keeps SERPs for only the most recent wave cannot check cannibalisation against its own back catalogue, and the gap is invisible until something ships.

stemmingBug.finding: The wave-3 keyword dedupe compared candidate keywords against claimed primaries and secondaries using Jaccard over raw tokens with no stemming. Singular/plural pairs therefore scored below the 0.75 rejection threshold: "gift" and "gifts" are different tokens, so an exact-match-modulo-plural keyword scored 0.60 and passed.
stemmingBug.impact: One row (best-online-gifts-for-girlfriend) was planned that duplicated a published post's declared secondary keyword. Caught by the writing agent at Phase 2, before any blog JSON was written.
stemmingBug.rescan: A stemmed re-scan of all 19 rows against 163 claimed terms from the 60 written posts found exactly one other row above 0.80: long-distance-birthday-gift-website (0.80 vs the secondary "long distance gifts website" of long-distance-relationship-gifts-online-free). Judged ACCEPTABLE - it narrows the generic claimed phrase with "birthday", and the post deliberately took the timing/midnight lane. ACTION: it must cross-link long-distance-relationship-gifts-online-free in the remediation pass.
stemmingBug.fixForNextWave: Stem tokens (strip trailing s/es, ies->y) before the Jaccard dedupe, and run the check against secondaryKeywords as well as primaries. Both checks are cheap; neither was done.
